chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: Who was in the San Francisco band
summary: Lee names his band's tenor player Woodman and trumpeter Bates and a woman pianist he picked up in San Francisco.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You mean the guy in San Francisco?
I don't even know. I don't have a clue who the guy was; he was there when you know, when we were working there, but you never really get a chance to know those people really well.

Oh, yeah -- that's an interesting question, because the only one that you would know of -- we called him Brother Woodman, and his name was William Woodman, but he was Brett Woodman's brother, you know, the Woodman family here in Los Angeles were good musicians. I think

Brett's dad played trombone, and the brother I'm speaking of -- his real name was William Woodman -- but he played tenor sax, and he's the one that was up north with me, and, you know, we had -- it was just a good band, you know, wasn't nothing sensational about the band, but it was just a band that worked a lot.
Who were the other members that I wouldn't know?

Well, the reason I say that you wouldn't know is because I can't even remember them, but there was a couple, I tell you, I got the -- piano player and the bass player, I got them in San Francisco, and the 3 of us went up -- the trumpet player, Woodman and myself -- and I can see the trumpet player, but I can't remember -- Bates. Oh, I knew it would come up. His name was Bates. The trumpet player was named Bates.

And for a while, there was a girl that played good piano in San Francisco, and we used her for a while. I can't recall her name; she played, as I used to say -- she'd open us and she played good piano for a woman, you know.
Ooo, you wouldn't don't say a thing like that, would you?
